Hi @rage.iz.me, thanks for your PR! I have the following suggestions:

- Change the screenshot to select the "Hosts" field. Explain that this filter will display IPv4/IPv6 addresses only. This is recommended for those who are interested in typical Internet traffic, and are not interested in Ethernet addresses for example (which are visible in your screenshot).
- Clarify that this dialog displays host names for each IP address in a capture file with a known host. This host is typically taken from DNS answers in a capture file. (This should address @moshekaplan request above I think.)
- If a host name is not known from the capture, it can also be populated based on a reverse DNS lookup. This requires the menu option View -> Name Resolution -> Resolve Network Addresses to be enabled (disabled by default). This *also* required Preferences -> Name Resolution -> Use an external network name resolver to be enabled (this is the default option).
- The resolved addresses in this dialog are not automatically updated as they become available. Users have to reopen the dialog when new names become available. For example, when the previously mentioned "Resolve Network Addresses" option is changed, or when new packets with DNS answers are captured.

I hope you can turn this into some text :-)

thanks @Lekensteyn - worked it out ) Could you please check once again?

@@ -104,7 +104,20 @@ Opens this section of the User’s Guide.
 
 === Resolved Addresses
 
-{missing}
+The Resolved Addresses window shows the list of resolved addresses and their host names. Users can choose the `Hosts` field to display IPv4 and IPv6 addresses only. In this case, the dialog displays host names for each IP address in a capture file with a known host. This host is typically taken from DNS answers in a capture file. In case of an unknown host name, users can populate it based on a reverse DNS lookup. To do so, follow these steps:
+
+. Enable `Resolve Network Addresses` in the menu:View[Name Resolution] menu as this option is disabled by default.
+
+. Select `Use an external network name resolver` in the menu:Preferences[Name Resolution] menu. This option is enabled by default.
+
+NOTE: The resolved addresses are not updated automatically after users change the settings. To display newly available names user have to reopen the dialog.
+
+The `Ports` tab shows the list of service names, ports and types. 
+
+Wireshark reads the entries for port mappings from the `hosts` service configuration files. See <<ChAppFilesConfigurationSection>> section for more information.
+
+.Resolved Addresses window
